clusters.name: Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within months: you leaned hard on Rafe when you began at the conservatory that September, a wrist injury stopped your playing in October and left you anxious and unable to function, you and Rafe clashed and he moved out in November, you were on your own and high, and by early 1992 you were lost and low with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry, too much moving at once. Your functioning fell and your anxiety rose through these months as the loss and your own trouble piled up together.

clusters.name: Winifred's bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002, within roughly two years: you were running out of steam for performing and less content by the month, you had a disastrous audition and were done with performing, you were on poor terms with family and friends, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in the fall of 2002, you met Marisol and moved to Fenwick in 2003, you split up within the year and sank into a deep depression once you were back in Thornbury that winter, you could not face your family and relied on friends instead. Your functioning fell, your anxiety rose, and your distance from family deepened through these years; your grandmother spent her final months at your mother's home in the fall of 2003 and died in February 2004, and the shifts in your relationships and your own trouble built across the time her illness reached toward its end.

clusters.name: Lorna's death, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you took four weeks building at Alder Creek with Silas that summer and were too drained for conversation with your mother, she pressed to visit you there and your anxiety rose, you kept the door shut on her when she came, and when you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound that August you stopped speaking to her; that silence held roughly a year. Your distance from your mother deepened sharply in those months, and within a few months of your grandmother's death your aunt Imogen had a stroke. The shifts in your family ties and your own retreat, alongside your move away and your grandmother's loss, mark a deepening in the family.

clusters.name: Jonah's marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and her family's closeness, within roughly two and a half years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, then in October 2019 Wren was swamped one thing after another with a street party, a fundraising dinner, and a drive to the lake for her mother's retirement; your anxiety rose as you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, Wren's family talks all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear, you were awake from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, and Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions with long quiet drives home afterward. Your symptoms and anxiety rose and your functioning fell across these months as Wren's family fusion and your own sleeplessness tangled together around the gatherings that autumn.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
